subject: Request: ClearWave uptime exhibit and order form language for enterprise MSA
messages:
From: Susan Li <susan.li@clearwave.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com>, ClearWave Procurement <procurement@clearwave.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: uptime exhibit & order form language for ClearWave enterprise MSA

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we move toward signature on the enterprise MSA, procurement has asked for a clearly scoped uptime exhibit and matching order form language that reflects our production requirements. High-level asks from our side: 

- Availability target: 99.95% monthly uptime for the API endpoints serving inference (we can discuss regional carveouts).
- Latency: p95 inference latency target of <200ms for standard payloads (50 tokens) for US regions — we understand there may be caveats for burst/failover scenarios.
- Credits/Remedies table that maps % availability to credit amounts; we prefer a simple three-band structure.
- Evidence/evidence paths: telemetry retention and sample reports we can point to during procurement review.
- Order form language that ties the above to the service description and includes any required exceptions for scheduled maintenance and cross-region failover.

We also need the addendum to reference the attached SOW attachments (onboarding runbook, telemetry spec) and the DPA/data residency clause — our legal will want to see how data is handled during KV cache and prefix caching.

Can you send a draft addendum + suggested order form text and an estimated procurement timeline? Ideally we can get a draft to our legal by EoD Thursday (28 Apr) so they can review ahead of our internal exec sign-off next week.

Appreciate it — happy to join a short call if useful.

—
Susan Li
Director, Procurement
ClearWave Health
procurement@clearwave.com
Attachment: none (will accept as separate files)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com>
To: Susan Li <susan.li@clearwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: uptime exhibit & order form language for ClearWave enterprise MSA

Susan —

Thanks, and great to line this up. Please find attached a first-pass draft of an SLA addendum and a suggested order form worksheet for procurement review. Highlights and open items are below.

Attachments included: 
- CW_SLA_Addendum_v0.1.docx (draft language for availability, latency SLOs, credits table, exceptions)
- OrderForm_ClearWave_v1.xlsx (populated with technical contact info and proposed SKU mapping)

Key points in the draft: 
- Availability: 99.95% monthly (standard) measured at the public API gateway level. Scheduled maintenance windows are excluded (2 hours per month standard; proposed notification >=48 hours).
- Latency: committed p95 <200ms for inference requests originating in the US region for payloads <=50 tokens using Redwood-hosted model variants. We added a carveout clause for cross-region failovers, burst overloads, and model-variant fallbacks — these will be treated as exceptions with a different credit schedule.
- Credits: three-band model (>=99.95 — no credits; 99.5–99.949 — 5% monthly credit; <99.5 — 15% monthly credit) — this is intentionally conservative; happy to discuss.
- Evidence: we included a telemetry/retention appendix reference; we can provide a monthly availability report and a retrospective incident summary for any credit-eligible month.

Open items we need from your side before v0.2: 
1) Confirmation on the acceptable scheduled maintenance window and blackout periods.
2) Whether ClearWave requires stricter residency guarantees for KV cache persistence during snapshot/backups (affects wording in the DPA cross-ref).
3) Any procurement formatting preferences for the credits table (percentage vs. dollar cap).

Proposed next steps: 
- Internal tech call: Karthik (infra) + Monica (CS) + ClearWave SRE to validate failover/latency assumptions (30 minutes) — proposed windows: Tue 27 Apr 10:00–12:00 PT or Wed 28 Apr 14:00–16:00 PT.
- If we align on the above, I’ll circulate v0.2 by EoD 28 Apr for your legal and procurement to review.
- We can route v0.2 via DocuSign once legal signs off.

[Attachment: CW_SLA_Addendum_v0.1.docx (docx)]
[Attachment: OrderForm_ClearWave_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

Thanks — I’ll hold the proposed slots and jump on the call if you confirm one.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: uptime exhibit & order form language for ClearWave enterprise MSA

Hannah / Monica —

Quick technical note after reviewing v0.1: we're comfortable committing to p95 <200ms for US-regional traffic under normal operating conditions, but we need clearer language around the allowed exception windows. Two specific asks for the drafting team: 

1) Explicitly enumerate burst and failover carveouts: e.g., traffic spikes due to client-driven traffic bursts, cross-region failovers where traffic is routed across AZ/region boundaries, and model-variant fallbacks. Right now v0.1 has a high-level carveout; we should add examples and a mechanism for how we measure (e.g., tag periods as "failover event" in the monthly report).

2) Consider a secondary credits schedule for carveout-caused breaches (smaller credit bands). Customers often prefer not to have a full-blown exception; offering a reduced-credit option makes the commercial ask more palatable. Proposed alternative: if breach is during an acknowledged failover or surge window, apply a reduced band (99.0–99.499 — 3% credit; <99.0 — 7% credit).

3) We should avoid absolute residency guarantees for in-memory KV cache persistence in the addendum wording; instead reference operational controls and provide evidence (audit logs) — legal can map this to the DPA.

I can join the SRE call and bring sample telemetry dashboards and a short note on regional placement recommendations.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Susan / team —

Thanks for aligning on the call earlier this week — appreciated the productive conversation. Attached is v0.2 of the SLA addendum and an updated order form. Summary of what changed based on our call and internal review: 

- Added explicit carveout examples for bursts, cross-region failover, and model-variant fallbacks. Those carveouts now map to a secondary (reduced) credit schedule as discussed.
- Clarified scheduled maintenance notification (48 hours standard; emergency maintenance with immediate notice and post-event report).
- Reworded residency language for in-memory KV/cache snapshots to reference operational controls and audit evidence rather than an absolute residency guarantee.
- Included telemetry appendix and a sample monthly availability report template for procurement review.

Next steps: 
1) Please review v0.2 and confirm any redlines by EoD Mon 3 May so legal can prepare the MSA package.
2) If approved, we will initiate DocuSign routing (link below) and schedule an engineering onboarding session within two weeks of signature.
